scope: 14 ranked trading repositories plus the classic FinRL predecessor checked through primary repositories, exact license blobs, release metadata and documentation. Broad capability scan, not an exhaustive scan of GitHub, source-code security audit, financial recommendation or trading authorization.

release_dates_unavailable: LEAN current engine identified by actual master commit rather than legacy release tags
coverage.lookup_failures: Initial public API calls for four repositories failed with URLError; specific-tag/commit retries succeeded. Backtesting.py and Backtrader had no GitHub release entries, so official PyPI metadata was used. QuantConnect getting-started primary-domain fetch timed out; official lean.io mirror and authentication page were read.

candidates.name: LEAN engine
candidates.best_use: Multi-asset event-driven historical simulation with explicit execution, fees and brokerage models.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 engine; QuantConnect CLI/account/data services have separate requirements.
candidates.offline: Engine and prepared local datasets can support disconnected backtests after separate packaging; the documented Lean CLI requires a paid organization and Docker.
candidates.existing_overlap: Ariadne has exact tables and local records, not a market-simulation engine.
risks: Do not equate the open-source engine with free CLI/cloud service access.
Data subscriptions and brokerage terms remain separate.
Master development is active; old GitHub release-page tags do not identify the current build.
candidates.deployment: CPU/.NET engine. Current source readme describes .NET 10 and Windows/Linux development routes. Existing Ariadne documentation records Docker as uninstalled; this scan did not repeat the host inventory or provision dependencies.
candidates.cost: On-demand CPU and local historical-data storage; direct-engine integration has upfront engineering cost. CLI membership, vendor data and live operation can add recurring costs.
candidates.adapter: Pinned offline job taking an approved strategy template plus immutable local data and producing fills/equity/cost/assumption artifacts; no broker adapter loaded.

candidates.name: NautilusTrader
candidates.best_use: Deterministic event-driven simulation and common strategy interfaces for later paper execution.
candidates.license: LGPL-3.0 license text; current README identifies LGPL-3.0-only compatibility.
candidates.offline: Historical replay can be local with preloaded data and instrument definitions. Live adapters require their venues and feeds.
candidates.existing_overlap: Adds trading-specific clocks, orders, fills and reconciliation beyond Ariadne's general task worker.
risks: Newest observed 2.0.0rc8 is a prerelease; upstream explicitly discourages release candidates for real-capital production.
Current latest docs describe 2.x while unqualified normal install selects stable 1.x; APIs differ.
Windows Server CI support does not qualify this particular Windows desktop.
candidates.deployment: Current 2.x docs specify Python 3.13–3.14 and Windows x64/Server 2022 CI; pinned wheels and all dependencies need appliance qualification.
candidates.cost: CPU replay and storage scale with tick/order-book history; live service would run continuously. No throughput or energy measurements were made.
candidates.adapter: Separate offline replay worker first; compare stable-line semantics with fixtures before considering any paper adapter.

release.note: Release notes say 28 October UTC, while publication metadata says 29 October. Stable 1.x remains separately available.

candidates.name: Qlib
candidates.best_use: Offline factor pipelines, model comparison and walk-forward quantitative research on prepared datasets.
candidates.license: MIT core; datasets and model/dependency assets have separate terms.
candidates.offline: Prepared data, features and locally trained models can be evaluated offline; data refresh and online services cannot.
candidates.existing_overlap: Adds financial-feature/model evaluation to Ariadne's existing exact analytics and document reports.
risks: Version 0.9.8 contains security hardening for executable recorder artifacts and configuration-driven local imports.
Untrusted serialized models, local Python configurations and arbitrary feature expressions must remain blocked.
Research performance does not establish a profitable day-trading strategy.
candidates.deployment: Python worker, CPU baseline before optional GPU. Dependency and model artifacts must be pinned separately from Ariadne's server environment.
candidates.cost: On-demand feature calculation and training; large experiments require bounded storage/CPU/GPU. No hosted model/API is inherently required for a local baseline.
candidates.adapter: Data-only factor evaluation with approved models, explicit train/validation/test boundaries and a signed-off trusted-artifact policy; no executable model imports from web sources.

candidates.name: VectorBT
candidates.best_use: Vectorized parameter exploration and portfolio visualizations on cached arrays.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 WITH Commons Clause; this is a sale-restricting source-available condition, not an unrestricted permissive default.
candidates.offline: Core array research can be local. Data downloads and external integrations still need connectivity.
candidates.existing_overlap: Adds financial strategy simulation/plots; basic exact aggregations are already present.
risks: Commons Clause restricts selling products/services deriving substantial value from the software; review the exact proposed business distribution.
PRO is a separate offering.
Large parameter sweeps can consume RAM and encourage overfitting.
candidates.deployment: Python/NumPy/Numba, with optional Rust kernels; Windows wheels/dependencies need qualification.
candidates.cost: On-demand CPU/RAM. Do not assume PRO functions are in the public package or that commercial use is automatically unrestricted.
candidates.adapter: Optional research comparator only after product-license review; avoid bundling as the default commercial appliance engine.

candidates.name: FinRL-X / FinRL-Trading
candidates.best_use: Compare modular financial ML/RL research pipelines and portfolio-weight contracts.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 in this separate repository; classic FinRL is MIT and remains educational/research software.
candidates.offline: Saved data/backtest stages can be local. Automatic providers, optional LLM preprocessing and Alpaca execution require their services.
candidates.existing_overlap: A research framework to evaluate against simpler deterministic baselines; not a replacement for Ariadne's authority and receipt system.
risks: Upstream describes production-oriented capabilities, but no independent qualification was performed here.
Portfolio-weight examples are not proof of intraday execution performance or returns.
Optional LLM/provider calls and broad model dependencies can raise cost and authority.
candidates.deployment: Python 3.11+ advertised; uses a bt-based backtest layer. GPU requirements depend on the selected training experiment.
candidates.cost: Potentially substantial training and dependency/storage cost; start with CPU baselines and no hosted LLM.
candidates.adapter: Offline frozen-dataset experiment runner, then paper-only comparison after an independently reviewed broker boundary.

candidates.name: OpenBB Open Data Platform
candidates.best_use: Normalize financial data providers for local research and provenance-rich market reports.
candidates.license: Current repository Apache-2.0; v5 notes explicitly record migration from AGPL-3.0-only. Data/vendor/Workspace terms are separate.
candidates.offline: Previously saved local data can be analyzed offline; fresh provider requests, entitlements and optional hosted products need connectivity.
candidates.existing_overlap: Adds finance-specific provider schemas instead of rebuilding every market-data adapter; existing Ariadne tables/reports can consume bounded exports.
risks: Canonical repository moved from OpenBB-finance/OpenBB to openbq-org/OpenBB.
OpenBB's broader suite/stewardship announcement is not evidence that every hosted feature is an offline Apache artifact.
GitHub latest release selector returned legacy ODP, while a separate openbb-v5.0.0 release exists: pin the exact package set.
candidates.deployment: Python data layer; fetch only a minimal set of reviewed providers in a separate worker. Do not add a second general AI frontend by default.
candidates.cost: Software itself adds no mandatory model subscription; vendor data, hosted Workspace, API quotas and maintenance may add costs.
candidates.adapter: Read-only provider ingestion into dated Parquet/CSV/JSON snapshots, hash/version/entitlement metadata and Ariadne research reports.

candidates.name: CCXT
candidates.best_use: Uniform cryptocurrency exchange market-data interfaces and later tightly scoped exchange adapters.
candidates.license: MIT core; individual exchange/data terms remain separate.
candidates.offline: Saved responses can be used offline, but this is an online exchange API library, not an offline market or backtester.
candidates.existing_overlap: Adds venue-specific normalization beyond generic HTTP integration; public-web GET tools cannot substitute for a complete market-data adapter.
risks: Market data can be delayed/incomplete and exchange APIs/rate limits change.
Live order/cancel/private-account calls must remain separate from read-only ingestion.
Cryptocurrency venue availability and product eligibility must be checked for the operator.
candidates.deployment: Python/Node and other clients; qualify only one language and a small exchange allowlist.
candidates.cost: Public API calls may have quotas; private trading has fees and possibly data charges. Adapters need continuing maintenance.
candidates.adapter: Initially public read-only market-data snapshots, explicit exchange/symbol/timeframe and request budgets; no API keys or order methods exposed to the model.

candidates.name: Hummingbot
candidates.best_use: Crypto market-making/execution research and later controlled paper experiments.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 core; gateway/connector/dependency and venue terms still need exact-artifact review.

candidates.name: Alpaca-py
candidates.best_use: Official Python SDK for later read-only broker data and explicitly chosen paper-account testing.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 SDK; broker account, market-data entitlements and service terms are separate.
candidates.offline: Broker/paper/data APIs require Internet and credentials; only separately saved snapshots are offline.
candidates.existing_overlap: Would add an actual broker connection; existing generic HTTP connectors do not provide its order reconciliation semantics.
risks: Paper and live credentials/endpoints must be structurally separated.
Paper fills omit market impact, latency slippage and queue position, among other effects.
Account/data eligibility and feeds must be confirmed; a free software license does not grant comprehensive realtime data.
candidates.deployment: Official SDK requires Python 3.10+; isolated adapter, no local broker software required by this SDK.
candidates.cost: SDK license fee is not the data/trading cost; account entitlements, data subscriptions, exchange/regulatory/trading fees may apply.
candidates.adapter: Read-only account snapshot first, then a dedicated paper credential/endpoint allowlist with bounded order intent and reconciliation.
